Hi Maya —

Appreciate the clear list. We're happy to provide the details and a short SRE call. I started filling the SLO/monitoring tab and attached a short guide with our standard definitions and telemetry access patterns. High-level answers below (I'll complete the worksheet and return as a marked-up file):

- SLOs: We maintain per-route SLOs. Availability is measured as successful 2xx/3xx responses from our ingress at the regional edge, evaluated as a rolling 30-day window. Typical availability target we offer for enterprise contracts is 99.9% for the inference API (endpoint-level SLA available via contract).
- Latency SLOs: By default we publish p95 and p99 for token generation latency over a rolling 7-day window (configurable in Dedicated/Private).
- Monitoring & retention: Metrics (Prometheus metrics ingested), traces (OpenTelemetry), and logs (structured request logs) are retained 90 days in the standard package; longer retention is available as an add-on.
- Customer access: We provide read-only Grafana dashboards via SSO (SAML/SCIM) and an exports API to pull aggregated SLO reports.
- Alerting: Customers receive SLA-impacting incident notifications via email and can subscribe to OpsPager (PagerDuty integration). For enterprise we offer a named on-call escalation path.
- Exceptions/custom SLAs: Any exceptions or contractual SLA changes must go through the account/procurement review; we capture them in a written amendment (process described below).

I'm cc'ing Karthik (SRE/Product) to confirm the measurement math and retention numbers and to provide the SSO/dashboard onboarding doc. I'll follow up with the completed worksheet and a couple of attachments.

Attachment: redwood-slo-guide.pdf (pdf)

Best,

2) Failure modes: does your availability calculation exclude scheduled maintenance and known degradations if we have a planned maintenance window?
3) Dashboards: can we get a read-only Grafana account scoped to only our org and to particular dashboards? Or is the recommended pattern for you to provide scheduled SLO reports (CSV) instead?

We might need to request an exception for a tighter availability target depending on contract negotiation. Also, we'd like to confirm how long historical latency histograms are stored (we use p99 over 30d for internal checks).

Hi Maya and Luke —

Thanks for the follow-ups — answers below and attached two short artifacts you can share with procurement/SRE: a one-page technical note (slo-definitions.csv) and our step-by-step dashboard access guide (metrics-access-setup-guide.pdf).

1) Measurement window and aggregation
- Availability: computed as successful responses / total requests at the regional edge using a sliding 30-day window (UTC-aligned). We compute per-region availability and report at both region and global levels; contractual SLA publishes the regional level by default.
- Latency: we store histograms and compute p95/p99 over configurable windows; by default p99 is computed as the 99th percentile of request latency over a rolling 7 or 30-day window depending on the metric.

2) Exclusions and scheduled maintenance
- Scheduled maintenance that is announced >=72 hours in advance and falls within an agreed maintenance outage window is excluded from availability calculations. Unplanned maintenance and customer-caused misconfigurations are not excluded.

3) Dashboards and metrics access
- We provide read-only Grafana access scoped to your org via SSO (SAML). Onboarding is self-serve with SCIM provisioning or we can create accounts for your SSO admin. Dashboards can be scoped to specific services and query parameters; customers may also request a monthly CSV export of SLO reports. Historical histogram buckets (raw) are retained 90 days by default; aggregated snapshots can be retained longer as an add-on.

4) Alerting & response
- Standard package: mean-time-to-first-response (MTTFR) for SLO-impacting incidents is typically under 60 minutes during business hours; for enterprise customers we offer a named on-call with 15–30 minute acknowledgement SLAs.

5) Exception/custom SLA requests
- To request a custom availability target (e.g., 99.95%) we require an SRE review and a written amendment. Typical lead time is 4–6 weeks to evaluate capacity/financial uplift and operational controls; pricing uplift depends on workload characteristics (token volumes, model size, retention, and cross-region requirements).

- If you'd like, we can set a 30-minute call with Karthik (cc'd) and our SRE lead to go over the measurement math and onboarding flow.
